car.name: Cars
car.intro: Explore a typical gasoline car. Layout and equipment vary by vehicle.
systems: A gasoline engine burns a controlled air-and-fuel mixture. Combustion pressure pushes pistons, which turn the crankshaft.
The transmission selects gear ratios so the engine can operate effectively at different road speeds. It passes torque into the driveline.
Driven by the engine, an alternator supplies electricity and helps recharge the battery while the engine is running.
The engine control module reads sensors and controls outputs such as fuel injection and ignition timing. Exact responsibilities vary by vehicle.
Friction brakes convert motion into heat as pads or shoes press against discs or drums.

diesel.name: Diesel trucks
diesel.intro: Explore the main systems of a typical heavy diesel truck.
systems: The engine compresses air until it becomes hot enough to ignite injected diesel fuel. Pistons and connecting rods turn the crankshaft.
Exhaust gas spins a turbine that drives an intake-air compressor. An intercooler commonly cools the compressed air before it reaches the engine.
Injectors deliver fuel into the cylinders at the required time and pressure. Fuel-system designs vary, including common-rail systems.
A manual uses driver-operated clutch and shift controls. An automated manual uses actuators to operate a similar clutch-and-gearbox arrangement.
A torque-converter automatic uses planetary gear sets and hydraulically applied friction elements to select ratios.
The engine control module uses sensors to manage fuel delivery and related systems.
Typical systems may include exhaust-gas recirculation, a diesel particulate filter and selective catalytic reduction. Equipment varies by engine and year.

ev.name: Electric vehicles
ev.intro: Explore a battery-electric vehicle. It does not use a gasoline engine or a conventional alternator.
systems: The high-voltage battery stores electrical energy used by the drive motor. A battery management system monitors conditions such as voltage and temperature.
Magnetic fields in the motor turn its rotor, delivering torque to the wheels through a reduction gear or other drive arrangement.
In a typical AC drive system, the inverter converts battery DC power into controlled AC power for the motor. It also supports regeneration.
An onboard charger converts AC supply power into DC for the battery. DC fast charging uses charging equipment outside the vehicle.
The converter steps down traction-battery voltage to supply lower-voltage systems and help maintain the auxiliary battery.
During regeneration, the drive motor acts as a generator, sending energy back toward the battery. Friction brakes still provide braking when needed.

boat.name: Boats
boat.intro: Explore a typical powered boat. Outboards, inboards and other installations have different layouts.
systems: The engine creates torque for the propulsion system. Marine installations use components and arrangements suited to operating around water.
The drive transfers engine torque to a propeller, which accelerates water and produces thrust. Some boats use waterjets instead.
Depending on the design, raw water cools the engine directly or removes heat through a heat exchanger in a closed cooling system.
Batteries, charging equipment and wiring supply the starter and onboard loads. Arrangements vary by engine and boat.
Mechanical or electronic controls manage throttle and gear selection. Engines with electronic control units also use sensors to manage operation.

motorcycle.name: Motorcycles
systems: Combustion turns the crankshaft. Motorcycles use a range of engine layouts, including single-cylinder, parallel-twin and inline-four designs.
The clutch allows the engine to be temporarily disconnected from the transmission for starting, stopping or gear changes.
A typical motorcycle gearbox uses sequentially selected gear ratios to match engine speed and wheel speed.
A chain, belt or shaft transfers power from the transmission to the driven wheel.
On electronically managed motorcycles, the control unit uses sensor information to manage fuel injection and other functions.
A typical stator generates AC electricity, and a regulator-rectifier converts and regulates it for the electrical system.
